messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finvault.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 14:23:00 -0700
Subject: Great meeting at AI Summit — quick recap + next steps

Hi Alex —

Great to meet you in person at the AI Summit yesterday. Thanks for walking me through FinVault's fraud-detection pipeline — really interesting work. As discussed, I wanted to summarize next steps so they are easy to reference: 

- Context: real-time scoring on transactional data, 250 req/s peak, 50ms 95th latency target for scoring.
- Current constraints: on-prem ETL, strict PII controls, procurement requires SOC2 and customer-managed KMS for keys.
- Redwood fit: low-latency GPU inference with private deployment options (VPC/on-prem), prefix caching for recurring session contexts, and quantization recommendations to reduce cost.

Proposed next steps:
1) Quick technical sync (30 min) with your infra/ML engineer to validate model compatibility and network requirements — are mornings PST next week possible?
2) I'll attach a short deck with our private deployment checklist and an example SLA/commit for Dedicated capacity.
3) I'll pull together SOC2 evidence and the contact for our security team if procurement wants to start the review.

Attaching: redwood-inference-sales-deck.pdf (2 slides on private deployment + sizing).

If you're swamped this week, happy to send a 1-pager instead. Would you like me to loop in Rachel Kim (Solutions Engineering) for the tech call?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

--
Redwood Inference — Make inference predictable and economical

Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Quick check — priority/timing for inference project at FinVault?

Alex —

Looping in Rachel from Solutions Engineering in case it helps to surface any technical blockers early. We've seen procurement timelines shift for a few banks after conferences, so I wanted to check whether this is a Q4 priority or something you're likely to push to next quarter. A few options that usually help customers move faster:

- Short technical deep-dive (30 min) to confirm model compatibility and network requirements.
- Trial proposal: 4-week Private eval on small footprint (we can scope 2 GPUs) to validate latency and integration.
- Pricing/commit framing: preliminary Dedicated pricing to fit your expected throughput; no legal overhead until you want to proceed.

If Q4 is realistic, we can prioritize a trial + SOC2 package. If not, happy to schedule a check-in for early October. Would you prefer Rachel or me to lead the tech call?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole

Hi Marissa —

Sorry for the slow reply; we've been buried with post-conference follow-ups and the fraud ops team is in a planning sprint. We are interested — the private eval sounds useful to validate latency against our on-prem data constraints. Procurement also flagged that SOC2 evidence will be required before any trial.

Can we aim for a tech sync the week of Oct 4? That gives our infra lead time to free up and for procurement to start the paperwork. If you can send the SOC2 pack and a short trial proposal today, I'll share with the team so we have materials ready for the Oct sync.

Best,
Alex
Head of ML Infrastructure, FinVault
